spec.description: Retrieve information about recent withdrawals. Results are sorted by recency; use the `cursor` parameter to iterate through the list of withdrawals (page size equal to the value of `limit`) from newest to oldest. Requires the `Funds permissions - Withdraw` or `Data - Query ledger entries` API key permission.

asset.description: Filter for a specific asset being withdrawn.

aclass.description: Filter for a specific asset class being withdrawn.

method.description: Filter for a specific name of withdrawal method.

start.description: Start timestamp; withdrawals created strictly before this will not be included in the response.

end.description: End timestamp; withdrawals created strictly after this will not be included in the response.

cursor.description: `true`/`false` to enable/disable the paginated response shape, or a cursor string (returned by a previous call) to fetch the next page. Default `false`.

anyOf.description: Cursor for the next page of results.

limit.description: Number of results to include per page.

rebase_multiplier.description: Optional parameter for viewing xstocks data. `rebased` displays in terms of underlying equity; `base` displays in terms of SPV tokens.

anyOf.description: Withdrawal records, returned when `cursor` is unset or `false`.

network.description: Network name based on the funding method used.

fee.description: Fees paid. Type inferred as `string` by analogy with every other `fee` field in this operation family, since upstream declares no `type` for this property.

time.description: Unix timestamp when the request was made.

status.description: Status of the withdrawal. See the IFEX financial transaction states reference linked from upstream docs for background.

status-prop.description: Additional status property, if available: `cancel-pending` (cancellation requested), `canceled`, `cancel-denied` (cancellation requested but denied), `return` (a return transaction initiated by Kraken; cannot be canceled), or `onhold` (pending review).

key.description: Withdrawal key name, as set up on the account.

anyOf.title: WithdrawStatusPage
anyOf.description: Paginated withdrawal results, returned when the `cursor` request parameter is set -- confirmed live; upstream's own OpenAPI schema only documents the bare-array shape for this endpoint (unlike deposit_status, which documents both).

next_cursor.description: Cursor to pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page of results. `null` once there is no further page -- confirmed live.

notes: Upstream `requestBody` requires `nonce`; dropped from this schema since the core's `authed_request` (`core/transport/http.py`) injects a strictly-increasing nonce into every private call automatically -- it is never a caller-supplied parameter, matching the existing hand-written `deposit_methods(self, asset)` signature, which takes none.

Same `cursor`/`limit` pagination prose as DepositStatus ("use the cursor parameter to iterate through list of withdrawals... from newest to oldest"), but unlike DepositStatus this operation's own response schema (`result`) never documents a `next_cursor` field at all -- only a bare array of withdrawal records, confirmed against the live doc page ("the result field is always a bare array... The documentation does not mention a next_cursor field"). That asymmetry with DepositStatus is upstream's, not introduced here. Left the response as the documented bare array and declared no `pagination` block, since where the next cursor value would come from is not stated anywhere machine-readable for this endpoint; needs a live call to settle before it can be specced.
